title: Add Reversed Digit Lists
statement:
Two non-negative whole numbers are stored as linked lists of digits, with the ones digit first. So [6, 4, 9] is the number 946. Neither list has extra zeros at the end, except the number 0 itself, which is [0].

Return their sum as a new list in the same format.

The numbers can have up to 100 digits, far more than a 64-bit integer holds.

examples.why: 946 + 78 = 1024. The lists have different lengths, and the last carry makes the answer one digit longer than either input.
10¹⁸ − 1 plus 1. Turning the lists into JavaScript numbers fails here: above 2⁵³ they cannot store every whole number, and the carry runs through all 18 digits.
0 + 35 = 35. Adding zero must not add a digit.

constraints: No list ends in 0 unless it is exactly [0]
hints: How did you add long numbers on paper in school? In which order did you visit the digits, and the lists already store them in that order.
Walk both lists together. Each step adds one digit from each (or 0 if a list has ended) plus the carry from the step before.
Keep going while either list has nodes or the carry is not zero. The digit to write is sum % 10 and the new carry is floor(sum / 10).

explain.intuition:
This is column addition from school. You start at the ones column, add the two digits and the carry, write down the last digit and carry the rest. Storing the ones digit first is what makes linked lists a good fit: the order you can walk a singly linked list is exactly the order the addition needs.

The tempting shortcut is to turn each list into a number, add, and turn the result back into digits. With up to 100 digits that breaks: a JavaScript number is exact only up to 2⁵³, about 16 digits. (Python's integers and JavaScript's BigInt have no such limit, so the shortcut does work with them, but an interviewer asking this wants the carry loop.)
steps: Create a dummy node and a tail pointer; set carry = 0.
Append a node with sum % 10, set carry = floor(sum / 10), and advance a and b if they are not null.
pitfalls: Stopping when both lists end and dropping the final carry: 5 + 5 would give [0] instead of [0, 1].
Stopping when the shorter list ends. The longer list's remaining digits still need the carry added to them.
Converting to a number. It is silently wrong past 16 digits.

solutions.title: Convert through a big integer
solutions.idea: Read each list into a big integer (BigInt in TypeScript, a plain int in Python), add, and write the digits back out ones-first. Works because these types have no size limit.

solutions.title: Column addition with a carry
solutions.idea: Walk both lists at once, adding digit + digit + carry. Keep going while either list has digits or a carry remains.
solutions.py:
class Solution:
    def addDigitLists(self, a: Optional[ListNode], b: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        dummy = tail = ListNode()
        carry = 0
        while a or b or carry:
            total = (a.val if a else 0) + (b.val if b else 0) + carry
            carry, digit = divmod(total, 10)
            tail.next = ListNode(digit)
            tail = tail.next
            a = a.next if a else None
            b = b.next if b else None
        return dummy.next

followups: The digits are stored the other way round, largest digit first. How do you add them without reversing the input lists?
Subtract instead of add, assuming a ≥ b. What replaces the carry, and how do you remove leading zeros from the result?
